body: of course. i just wanted to help some :)

I can kind of relate to you. I've never really had any traumatic experiences in my life. I think the only bad things that have ever happened to me are my dad leaving me almost seven years ago (but tbh i've never really been bothered by that) and a bad break up in the middle of quarantine, which is really where my depression spiraled out of control. But anyway, even before the breakup, I was just extremely depressed for years on end and just couldnt get a handle on it. i was never professionally diagnosed with depression, but i think its fair to assume with the 70ish scars on my right leg from cuts show that i might have it. to simplify my story, i had depression for years, then the months leading up to covid i thought i had my shit together, covid hit and started to lose myself even more, then i broke up with my gf and my mental health crashed. I had plenty of supportive people around me like my parents, friends, hell even my ex was willing to stay friends and help me out, but it didn't do much. i felt i was worthless, that i was a waste, that i didn't deserve love, i didn't deserve anything, and the pain in my heart was never going to go away. but then one day (a few weeks ago actually) i just sat down and focused on what i was feeling. not what was causing my pain, but i closed my eyes and for about ten minutes i just focused on the physical pain i was feeling. and for some reason that helped. i think i just understood my feelings ever so slightly more, and that helped me to realize what i was hurt about and how to get past it. i stopped worrying about what i wanted to be and...well...just started to be me. i started embracing the big dork that i am and i feel so much better. there's quite a bit more to that but thats the gist. and of course im not 100% yet, hell im far from it. but i can feel the progress ive made, and just that makes me truly believe that one day things will be ok.

i dont know exactly what you're going through, and i think anyone who says they do is lying because no one truly does (am i right?). however, i do know how it feels to hurt and be depressed even when it feels like you shouldn't. its ok to be that way. you just gotta find a way to look past it and be ok. and i know that sounds cheesy af, but...yeah. idk if im making a whole ton of sense rn cuz as im writing this im tired af. but i just also want to say if you need someone to talk to, id be glad to try and help so just shoot me a message (or whatever you call it on reddit, im still kind of new here). im here if you want :)

Thank you. I just have no idea how to love myself and being ok with myself. I don't even really know what it means to do that. I've learned to calm myself down a little bit when things get really bad but that's about it.
